topic_tag: a reform newspaper and the shorter-hours movement
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: Weighing its influence, one historian called the weekly newspaper the shorter-hours movement's ______.

worlds.passage: In the 1870s, factory workers campaigned for a shorter working day, and one weekly newspaper was closely tied to their movement. Its sellers worked factory gates in towns the movement had never reached, and the movement's register shows a new branch forming in each such town within months of the first copies arriving. The editors printed reports sent in by the branches but never an editorial, and by 1880 most branches had their own halls and treasuries. Weighing its influence, one historian called the weekly newspaper the shorter-hours movement's ______.
worlds.explanation: New branches formed wherever the paper's sellers went, so it drove the movement's growth and was its "engine." "Compass" fails because it never printed an editorial. "Crutch" fails because the branches soon had their own halls and treasuries, and "epilogue" fails because it was spreading the movement while the movement was growing.

compass.why: A paper that set out no views gave the movement no direction.

crutch.why: Self-supporting branches did not lean on the paper.

epilogue.why: The paper was active while the movement was still growing.

worlds.passage: In the 1870s, factory workers campaigned for a shorter working day, and one weekly newspaper was closely tied to their movement. Its few hundred copies went only to the movement's committee, and the committee's minutes show it voting again and again to target the factories and press for the laws that the latest editorial had proposed. The paper closed in 1881, and the committee's campaigns over the next twenty years followed the program set out in its last issues. Weighing its influence, one historian called the weekly newspaper the shorter-hours movement's ______.
worlds.explanation: The committee steered by the paper's editorials and kept to its program long after it closed, so it was the movement's "compass." "Engine" fails because its few copies went only to the committee. "Crutch" fails because the movement carried on for twenty years without it, and "epilogue" fails because it shaped campaigns while they were being fought.

engine.quote: went only to the movement's committee
engine.why: A paper that reached no one outside the committee did not drive growth.

crutch.why: The movement did fine without it, so it had not been leaning on it.

epilogue.why: The paper was guiding live campaigns, not looking back on finished ones.

worlds.passage: In the 1870s, factory workers campaigned for a shorter working day, and one weekly newspaper was closely tied to their movement. The movement owned no press and kept no treasury of its own; it printed its notices and paid its organizers out of the paper's subscriptions, which came almost entirely from its own members. The paper took positions on nothing, and after its printer went bankrupt in 1881 the branches, unable to announce a meeting or pay a speaker, had dissolved within the year. Weighing its influence, one historian called the weekly newspaper the shorter-hours movement's ______.
worlds.explanation: The movement depended on the paper for printing and money and dissolved once it failed, so the paper was its "crutch." "Engine" fails because its subscribers were almost all existing members. "Compass" fails because it took positions on nothing, and "epilogue" fails because it was the movement's support while the movement was active.

engine.quote: almost entirely from its own members
engine.why: A paper read only by existing members did not drive growth.

epilogue.why: It sustained the movement while it was active.

worlds.passage: In the 1870s, factory workers campaigned for a shorter working day, and one weekly newspaper was closely tied to their movement. Its first issue appeared in 1879, the year after the last mill accepted the shorter day and the movement's branches voted to disband. For a decade it printed recollections and obituaries of former members and notices of their reunions, and its circulation fell each year as its readers aged. Weighing its influence, one historian called the weekly newspaper the shorter-hours movement's ______.
worlds.explanation: Founded after the movement had won and disbanded, and given over to recollections and obituaries, the paper was the movement's "epilogue." "Engine" and "crutch" fail because the movement had already won before the paper appeared. "Compass" fails because a paper of recollections and obituaries set no direction.

engine.quote: the movement's branches voted to disband
engine.why: A paper that began after the movement ended could not drive it.

crutch.quote: the year after the last mill accepted the shorter day
crutch.why: The movement had already succeeded without the paper.

compass.quote: recollections and obituaries of former members
compass.why: Looking back set no course for anyone.
